name: Kang-Petrov Arms KP-9T 'Thinline'
description:
The KP-9T is a single-stack 9x19mm concealment pistol built on a chassis that is, by design, almost aggressively uninteresting. Where other manufacturers chase slim profiles with exotic alloys or printed ceramics, Kang-Petrov achieved the KP-9T's 22mm width through the brutally practical approach of simply removing everything that wasn't load-bearing. No accessory rail. No ambidextrous controls. No grip texture beyond a simple stipple pattern applied at the factory. The result is a 15-round single-stack pistol that disappears into a waistband, pocket, or thigh rig with minimal printing, runs standard 9x19mm brass or caseless interchangeably, and costs less than a week's groceries for a mid-tier wage.

The Thinline was designed explicitly for the Gray Zone worker who rides public transit, who can't afford the social cost of printing a full-size under a work jacket, and who needs something that doesn't scream 'armed' to Arcturus patrols that have standing authority to detain anyone presenting as a threat. It sells in enormous volumes in the residential blocks between industrial zones—places where the walk from the mag-rail station to the apartment block covers three different territorial boundaries and two hours of low-light. The KP-9T is honest about what it is: a last-resort tool for people who can't afford to be obviously armed.

Most Thinlines that see real use develop a characteristic wear pattern—the right side of the slide polishes bright from draw-stroke friction against belt loops or waistband fabric, while the grip stipple smooths out over months of carry. Old hands in the the Gray Zone districts can clock a Thinline by the sound of it coming out of a pocket holster: a dry whisper, almost nothing. The gun doesn't ask much of you. It asks you to point it at the problem and pull the trigger, and it will do the rest.
specifications: caliber: 9x19mm Standard / 9x19mm Caseless effective_range: 35m rate_of_fire: Semi-automatic magazine_capacity: 15 rounds weight: 0.61 kg
tactical_use: The KP-9T is purpose-built for deep concealment and close-range defensive use. Most engagements it's used in are under 10 meters. The slim profile means two-handed shooting requires a slight grip adjustment, and shooters with larger hands often find the factory grip too short for a full purchase—a problem Kang-Petrov addressed with an optional extended baseplate that adds two rounds and a finger groove. Operators who run it seriously practice one-handed shooting from retention, since the gun's size and context mean drawing room is rarely ideal.
cultural_context: The KP-9T has a complicated reputation in GLMZ. Arcturus patrols associate it with the Gray Zone workers who are trying to hide something, even though the gun is fully legal and standard-registered. There's a persistent myth that the Thinline has a 'poor person's trigger'—a rougher pull, a heavier reset—compared to the KP-19. This is not true. The myth persists because of who carries it, not how it shoots.
known_users: the Gray Zone workers in high-transit areas
low-tier medical workers in Excluded zones
story_hooks: A KP-9T is recovered from a storm drain near a Slagworks administrative building — registered to a woman who died in an industrial accident three years ago, but the maintenance log shows it was cleaned and loaded within the week. Her family insists she had no enemies. Her former shift supervisor has recently taken a promotion.

Kyle Corbin-Vasik is asked to deliver a sealed package to an address in the South Residential blocks. The contact at the other end opens it to find a brand-new Thinline and a note in a handwriting Kyle doesn't recognize that says 'you'll need this before the vote.'
